title: Roadmap Linker: Lightweight Dependency Contracts and Escalation Bus
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight 'Linker' system to formalize cross-team roadmap contracts, produce actionable signals for planners, and provide an automated escalation bus for stuck or risky dependencies. The goal is a low-friction MVP that lives in Linear + Console dashboards and reduces missed handoffs between Eng/Design/Security/Infra during planning cycles.
comments: 2025-03-02 - Kickoff: PM, Eng (Luca), Design (Maya), Security (Jon) aligned on scope. Agreed MVP fields: owner, requested-by, earliest-blocking-date, requested-latency, risk-score, escalation-channel. Decided to avoid full dependency graph automations in v1.

2025-03-04 - Eng feasibility: ENG tech spike found two integration paths: (A) Linear custom fields + webhook enrichment; (B) small service in console that syncs with Linear. Luca prefers (B) for richer telemetry; tradeoff is infra work and auth surface area.

2025-03-06 - Design review: Presented wireframes for in-issue contract card and a minimal dashboard showing outstanding contracts by cycle. Designers requested an explicit "commit window" UI and a one-click escalate CTA. Action: DES to provide final card spec by 2025-03-11.

2025-03-09 - Security notes: Jon flagged that escalation bus must support audit logs and be configurable for teams with stricter routing (e.g., legal/security). Security review required for any automatic email/slack escalation. Scoped to manual escalation on v1 with audit trail capture.

2025-03-11 - PM decision: Move forward with service-based approach (Console sync). Rationale: enables signal enrichment (latency histograms, owner oncall), simpler rollout (feature flag), and better observability; added one sprint of infra effort to estimate.

2025-03-13 - Dev sync: ENG tasks split into API (create/update contract), background sync worker (pull Linear issues), and console UI components. PR template and contract schema drafted: fields limited to strings/dates/enums to keep frontend simple.

2025-03-14 - Design deliverable: Maya uploaded final card spec and interaction notes: include inline edit, history timeline, and lightweight commit badge when both teams accept contract. Link: https://drive.google.com/roadmap-linker-design-v1

2025-03-15 - PM review: Added success metrics and acceptance criteria; asked Eng to include telemetry hooks for 'time-to-accept' and 'escalation-rate'. Luca to attach instrumentation tasks to ENG-30412.

2025-03-17 - Blocker noted: Availability of Linear API rate limits for large orgs. Eng to open support ticket with Linear and add retry/backoff for sync worker. Temporary mitigation: pilot with 3 teams only.
2025-03-18 - Decision log: Pilot scope confirmed: Platform, Payments, Console infra. Rollout plan approved. Next steps: finish API, wire up UI, and run a 3-week pilot in Cycle 2025-W12.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A contract card can be created/edited in Linear and is visible in Console with consistent fields (owner, requested deliverable, target date, escalation SLA).
AC-2: Console dashboard surfaces outstanding contracts with filters by team, cycle, and risk-score.
AC-3: Manual escalation flow triggers a recorded audit event and sends a configurable Slack notification to the designated channel.
AC-4: Telemetry captured: time-to-accept, percent-accepted-before-target, escalation-rate; first-pass dashboards populated.
AC-5: Security sign-off obtained for audit log format and escalation channels (security_review_required = true).
success_metrics: SM-1: Reduce missed handoffs in pilot teams by 40% in next cycle (tracked via post-cycle retro and missed-deliverables tag).
SM-2: Average time-to-accept contract <= 7 days for high-priority items during pilot.
SM-3: Escalation noise: fewer than 1 false-positive escalation per 50 contracts in pilot.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): 3 teams (Platform, Payments, Console infra) opt-in for 3-week pilot in cycle 2025-W12.
Phase 1: Expand to product teams that cross >1 org boundary after pilot sign-off and fixed issues.
Phase 2: Default enable with onboarding tooltips and migration checklist in next quarter.
Rollout controls: feature-flagged service, per-team escalation config, and ability to opt-out.
notes: MVP will intentionally limit contract metadata to reduce cognitive load. Long-term roadmap may add automated critical-path detection, dependency graph visualization, and integration with Optimize for cost-aware prioritization. Keep API surface minimal for first release.
